course_name_en: Sensor Technology, Actuator Technology and Multifunctional Materials
prerequisites: Successful completion of the modules to be completed in the 1st and 2nd semesters according to the study plan.
Basic knowledge of mathematics, mechanics and materials science as taught in the lectures of the mechanical engineering basic course.
For 'Sensorik und Aktorik': Basic knowledge of mathematics, mechanics, measurement technology and electrical engineering as taught in the lectures of the mechanical engineering basic course.
For 'Multifunktionale Materialien': Basic knowledge of mathematics, mechanics, electrical engineering and materials science as taught in the lectures of the mechanical engineering basic course.

learning_outcomes.text: Students acquire basic knowledge of the use of sensors and actuators in mechatronic systems.
Students have an overview of various components in the field of sensors and actuators as well as their integration into higher-level overall systems.
Based on the fundamentals of materials science, students have an overview of the most important multifunctional materials, their functional mechanisms and application limits.
Students are able to recognise possible scenarios for the sensible use of these materials.
Students are able to design components for specific applications.
Students are able to verify the function of components by calculation.

syllabus_topics: Importance of sensory and actuating components in mechanical engineering
Methods of common measured value recording methods and actuators
Physical sensors (temperature sensors, derived measurement methods, pressure sensors, acceleration sensors, environmental sensors, optical sensors, chemical sensors)
Principles used in actuators (classification, characterization, modeling, control)
Practical examples of actuators (classic electric motors, moving coil actuators, piezoelectric actuators)
Development of causal relationships and components of a mechatronic system in a team
Presentation of results in a group lecture (Sensorik und Aktorik)
Introduction to the field of multifunctional materials (smart materials)
Structural properties of modern materials for mechanical support, sensory or actuator tasks
Influence of electrical, magnetic or thermal field variables on mechanical properties (Young's modulus, viscosity)
Basics of extraction, production, processing of materials
Functional mechanisms and calculation bases of piezoelectric materials
Functional mechanisms and calculation bases of thermal shape memory materials
Functional mechanisms and calculation bases of magnetic shape memory materials
Functional mechanisms and calculation bases of magnetic materials (e.g., magnetorheological fluids)
Technical applications of multifunctional materials through selected examples
assessment_rules: The module examination is an oral examination lasting 45-60 minutes. Students should be able to reproduce, explain, and apply the essential basics of sensors, actuators, and multifunctional materials, as well as their functionalities and applications. The credit points are awarded if the module examination is passed. The module examination can only take place after both parts of the module ('Sensorik und Aktorik' and 'Multifunktionale Materialien') have been completed.
